Jake — thanks, we got the traces and this is a good starting point. Quick clarifying Qs before we draft a recommended fleet:
1) Which models (exact checkpoints) do you expect to lock on Day 1 vs. likely to change during rollout? Large context (16k) usage is the driver for memory vs throughput tradeoffs.
2) Preferred procurement cadence (PoC -> Reserved 12m commit -> expand) and any hard sku constraints (gov/cloud region, on-prem)?
3) Do you have a target committed spend or preferred cost per 1M tokens cap? That helps balance H100 vs A100.

High-level, our past experience suggests a three-tier pool works best for mixed workloads:
- H100 (high-memory, best for large-context 70B / 80B models + multi-GPU sharding when needed)
- A100 (general purpose: strong FP16 perf and good memory for 30–40B models)
- L4 (cost-efficient int8 quantized inference for low-latency small prompts & embeddings)

I'll loop in Laura and Logan to run a quick sizing pass on the traces and produce a recommended fleet mix and fallback routing policy. If you can answer the three quick items above we can refine numbers.

If helpful I can also propose a PoC configuration that runs in our Hosted environment (fastest time-to-value) and then map that to Dedicated reserved sizing.

Aditya / team — I ran the supplied traces through our workload analyzer (see attached summary sheet: initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx). Key observations:
- Long-context requests (16k) are ~8% of traffic but dominate memory requirements. These map best to H100s when using 70B+ models unless you shard/model-slice.
- The bulk (≈72%) of requests are short to mid-length (<=1.2k tokens) where L4 quantized endpoints can handle inference at ~4–6x lower $/token with sub-100ms median latency for small prompts.
- A100s are the sweet spot for 30–40B production models that need a balance of memory and raw throughput.

Preliminary Dedicated fleet recommendation (steady-state estimates for production):
- 3 x H100 (for 16k context 70B instances + burst capacity for large-batch offline jobs)
- 6 x A100 (serve 30–40B production models + most of the live traffic)
- 10 x L4 (quantized low-cost endpoints for small prompts and embeddings; also used as overflow fallback)

Routing & ops notes:
- KV / prefix caching for conversational flows will reduce H100 pressure by ~15–25% for repeated context patterns; enable prefix caching on routes handling summarization.
- Autoscale policy: keep a small warm pool (10–15%) per pool to meet p50 latency SLOs; use burst capacity gating for A100 -> H100 fallback for large-batch jobs.
- Quantization/accuracy: push L4 for deterministic short-response use-cases (search, structured replies) but use A100/H100 for RLHF-fine-tuned variants where quality matters.

Rough cost ballpark (monthly infra-only, region: us-west):
- 3 H100 ~= $XXk/mo
- 6 A100 ~= $YYk/mo
- 10 L4 ~= $ZZk/mo
Total infra: ~${TOTAL_EST}k/mo (high-level estimate, we will refine with real pricing).

Next steps:
1) Confirm which exact model checkpoints you'll use Day 1 (helps refine memory per-instance).
2) Decide PoC cadence (we recommend Hosted PoC running 2 x A100 + 3 x L4 for 2 weeks to validate latency and cost before committing).
3) If you want, Marissa can prepare a Reserved pricing draft for a 12-month commitment (includes burst and SLAs).

Phased deployment proposal:

Phase 1 — Dedicated initial reserved (first 90 days): 3 x A100 + 5 x L4; configure route-based caching and warm-pool sizing to meet latency SLOs.
Phase 2 — Full Dedicated steady-state (12 month commit): 3 x H100, 6 x A100, 10 x L4 (as Laura suggested). Add burst policy to allow A100 -> H100 escalation for large-batch jobs and to handle 16k context peaks.

Procurement / compliance notes:
- SOC 2: we will share the SOC 2 Type II certificate & the external pen-test summary — Marissa will attach the pack.
- KMS options: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) in major clouds and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For PHI we recommend Private (VPC) Dedicated with KMS + audit logs enabled.
- Pricing: Marissa will provide a 12-month reserved pricing sheet + a hosted payg alternative (we'll include estimated infra-only numbers and an option with managed SLAs).

Operational considerations:
- Enable prefix/KV caching on summarization routes to reduce H100 load by estimated 15–25%.
- Instrument token-level tracing and prompt-set regression alerts during PoC to catch any model-quality regressions when moving to L4 quantized endpoints.
